item.title: San Francisco enfrenta una amenaza de inundación histórica ante la llegada de una gran tormenta
item.description: Las advertencias llegan en la semana del Día de Acción de Gracias y apenas unos días después de que una fuerte tormenta inundara las calles de San Francisco, dejando varados a los vehículos, obligando ...
item.dc:creator: Michael B. Marois, Jorgelina Do Rosario
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — San Francisco se prepara para una inundación costera que podría ser histórica esta semana, ya que las mareas inusualmente altas y una tormenta que se aproxima amenazan con inundar las calles y los barrios más bajos durante el ajetreado período de viajes del Día de Acción de Gracias. El Servicio Meteorológico Nacional advirtió que los niveles de agua en la Bahía de San Francisco podrían acercarse a los récords establecidos hace más de cuatro décadas, y se espera que la mayor amenaza de inundación se presente el martes y el miércoles. Los meteorólogos indicaron que el agua podría elevarse hasta 2,8 pies por encima del nivel del suelo en las zonas costeras vulnerables, lo que podría obligar a cerrar carreteras y dañar la infraestructura. El Aeropuerto Internacional de San Francisco se está preparando para inundaciones que podrían afectar los viajes durante una de las semanas más concurridas del año. Las autoridades del aeropuerto han despejado las zonas de drenaje, revisado las estaciones de bombeo y colocado sacos de arena y barreras portátiles contra inundaciones en lugares vulnerables, según el portavoz Doug Yakel. El aeropuerto espera recibir 6,7 millones de pasajeros entre el Día de Acción de Gracias y el Día de Año Nuevo, lo que representa un aumento del 8% con respecto al año pasado. VER MÁS: Las negociaciones de la ONU sobre el clima fracasan después de que los países rechacen el acuerdo “Incluso llegar al aeropuerto podría ser un reto. Esperamos que se cierren muchas carreteras”, dijo Dylan Flynn, meteorólogo del Servicio Meteorológico Nacional. “Y, por supuesto, es la semana de Acción de Gracias, así que hay más tráfico aéreo, y estas mareas ocurren en el peor momento posible”. Las advertencias llegan apenas unos días después de que una fuerte tormenta inundara las calles de San Francisco, dejando varados a los vehículos, obligando a cerrar carreteras y causando daños a los negocios. Las aguas de la inundación se desbordaron en el Embarcadero, cerca del famoso Ferry Building, mientras que el sistema de drenaje de la ciudad se vio desbordado por las fuertes lluvias. La amenaza se extiende a lo largo de gran parte de la costa de California, y los meteorólogos federales han emitido avisos y alertas de inundaciones costeras desde el condado de Humboldt, en el norte, hasta el condado de Los Ángeles, en el sur. El Servicio Meteorológico Nacional advirtió que las olas podrían alcanzar los 20 pies en algunas zonas de la Costa Central, mientras que las autoridades de San Diego están reforzando las barreras de las playas y preparándose para posibles cierres de carreteras. Una advertencia de inundación costera que abarca las costas de San Francisco y la Bahía de San Pablo entrará en vigor el lunes a las 6 a. m. y se mantendrá hasta las 4 p. m. del jueves, Día de Acción de Gracias. VER MÁS: Una tormenta arrasa un pueblo rural brasileño y pone en peligro los cultivos La amenaza de inundación se debe a una combinación de mareas excepcionalmente altas, conocidas como «mareas gigantes», marejadas ciclónicas y la expansión del agua de mar asociada a condiciones oceánicas inusualmente cálidas. El servicio meteorológico indicó que esta combinación podría elevar los niveles del agua a alturas poco comunes en la región. Según el servicio meteorológico, se prevé que los niveles de agua en el mareógrafo de San Francisco alcancen los 8,4 pies el martes por la mañana y alcancen su punto máximo de 8,6 pies el miércoles alrededor de las 10:49 a. m. Estas proyecciones se acercan al récord de 8,66 pies registrado en enero de 1983. “La bahía no suele subir tanto. Solo ha pasado un par de veces en la historia”, dijo Flynn. “Así que sí, esta es una amenaza significativa de inundación”. El alcalde de San Francisco, Daniel Lurie, instó el viernes a los residentes a tomar en serio las advertencias y a considerar evitar los desplazamientos no esenciales desde el lunes por la tarde hasta el miércoles, citando la posibilidad de inundaciones sin precedentes. Se espera que la tormenta traiga períodos de lluvias intensas el martes y el miércoles, lo que podría agravar las inundaciones, ya que las mareas excepcionalmente altas restringen el drenaje hacia la bahía. El servicio meteorológico indicó que la amenaza de inundaciones costeras podría persistir hasta el Día de Acción de Gracias, aunque se espera que las lluvias disminuyan a última hora del miércoles y que las condiciones se mantengan mayormente secas el jueves. item.title: San Francisco Faces Historic Flood Threat as Major Storm Nears
item.description: San Francisco is bracing for potentially historic coastal flooding this week as unusually high tides and an approaching storm threaten to inundate roads and low-lying neighborhoods during the busy Thanksgiving travel period.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- San Francisco is bracing for potentially historic coastal flooding this week as unusually high tides and an approaching storm threaten to inundate roads and low-lying neighborhoods during the busy Thanksgiving travel period.The National Weather Service warned that water levels in San Francisco Bay could approach records set more than four decades ago, with the greatest flooding threat expected Tuesday and Wednesday. Forecasters said water could rise as much as 2.8 feet above ground level in vulnerable coastal areas, potentially forcing road closures and damaging infrastructure.San Francisco International Airport is preparing for flooding that could disrupt travel during one of the busiest weeks of the year. Airport officials have cleared drainage areas, checked pumping stations and positioned sandbags and portable flood barriers in vulnerable locations, according to spokesperson Doug Yakel. The airport expects 6.7 million passengers between Thanksgiving and New Year’s Day, an 8% increase from last year.“Even getting to the airport could be a challenge. We’re expecting a lot of road closures,” said Dylan Flynn, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service. “And of course, it’s Thanksgiving week, so there’s higher flight traffic, and these tides happen at the worst possible time.”The warnings come just days after a powerful storm flooded streets across San Francisco, stranding vehicles, forcing road closures and damaging businesses. Floodwaters spilled onto the Embarcadero near the famous Ferry Building, while the city’s drainage system was overwhelmed by heavy rainfall.The threat extends along much of California’s coastline, with federal forecasters issuing coastal flood advisories and watches from Humboldt County in the north to Los Angeles County in the south. The National Weather Service warned that waves could reach 20 feet along parts of the Central Coast, while San Diego officials are reinforcing beach barriers and preparing for possible road closures.A coastal flood warning covering the San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines takes effect Monday at 6 a.m. and runs through 4 p.m. Thursday, Thanksgiving Day.The flooding threat stems from a combination of exceptionally high tides, known as king tides, storm surge and the expansion of seawater associated with unusually warm ocean conditions. The weather service said the combination could push water levels to heights rarely seen in the region.At San Francisco’s tide gauge, water levels are forecast to reach 8.4 feet Tuesday morning and peak at 8.6 feet Wednesday at about 10:49 a.m., according to the weather service. The projections approach the record of 8.66 feet recorded in January 1983.“The bay doesn’t get this high very often. It’s only happened a couple times in history,” Flynn said. “So yeah, this is a significant flooding threat.”San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie urged residents Friday to take the warnings seriously and consider avoiding nonessential travel from Monday afternoon through Wednesday, citing the potential for unprecedented flooding.The storm is expected to bring periods of heavy rain Tuesday and Wednesday, potentially worsening flooding as exceptionally high tides restrict drainage into the bay.The weather service said the coastal flooding threat could persist through Thanksgiving, although rain is expected to taper off late Wednesday and conditions should remain mostly dry Thursday.More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

FAST

CALGARY, Canada, Nov 22 : Focusing on the legacy of the Women's World Cup should be the top priority for those organising the 2031 and 2035 tournaments, according to a sports executive behind the 2023 competition. In Zurich on Monday, FIFA will confirm that the United States, Jamaica, Costa Rica and Mexico will host in 2031, with England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland on co-hosting duties in 2035. Unlike Australia and New Zealand in 2023, there will be 48 teams rather than 32, streaming giant Netflix will have some involvement and the tournaments will be held in markets more mature in terms of women's soccer development than Australia. But for James Johnson, who was the CEO for Football Australia between 2020 and 2025 and is now the commissioner of the Canadian Premier League, legacy remains the fundamental driving force administrators should be thinking about.

"If you're focused on legacy, I think it helps the tournament," he told Reuters by Zoom from Calgary, Canada, after writing a book on his 2023 experience, "Hosting the World". "In Australia it was about moving the sport from a fourth, fifth or even sixth-tier sport into the mainstream, and we were able to accomplish that. "It is a different market for 2031 and 2035. But the legacy conversation starts as soon as the hosting is officially awarded to those countries." An imperative for Johnson in 2023 was that the Matildas made it to the last weekend of the tournament, something he ensured by fighting for long-term funding for the team. Getting to the third-placed playoff meant many weeks of exposure for women's soccer in a country more traditionally interested in cricket and rugby. 'BETTER OPPORTUNITIES' And although it has received some criticism elsewhere for diluting quality, Johnson believes the expansion to 48 teams for 2031 and 2035 provides an opportunity for the host countries to spend more time in the limelight. "The additional content, the additional matches, what I hope it translates into is better opportunities for the home teams because that's really the amplifier of culture and the amplifier of interest in the tournaments," he said. "A host nation taking the tournament by storm and staying in there from start to finish is a key for the success of the tournament - and the cultural impact you create as a result." Next year's Women's World Cup in Brazil will include the involvement of a major streamer for the first time, with Netflix securing rights in the US and Canada for that tournament and the 2031 competition, as well as expressing interest in the 2030 men's World Cup. Ahead of the 2023 World Cup FIFA were critical of some traditional broadcasters – especially in Europe – for what they said was an undervaluation of women's soccer. But while Johnson welcomed the arrival of Netflix, he cautioned against the long-term danger of locking out potential viewers who had previously watched on free-to-air. "It creates a new dynamic, it's interesting, it's healthy for the sport because there's more competitions," he said. "What I hope it doesn't do though is put too much content behind paywalls because I think the beauty of a World Cup is the community that it creates, and the buzz that it creates, and the ability to bring people together, which means it needs to be widely distributed."

Source: Reuters

The spacecraft BepiColombo is seen at the European Space Agency's (ESA) European Space Research and Technology Centre (ESTEC) in Noordwijk, Netherlands July 6, 2017. REUTERS/Michael Kooren

FAST

Nov 22 : After an eight-year journey, the European-Japanese spacecraft BepiColombo has begun orbiting the solar system's smallest and innermost planet Mercury, though the European Space Agency said on Sunday a glitch has occurred involving its thrusters. Mercury, only slightly larger than Earth's moon, is the least explored of the four planets in the inner solar system, with BepiColombo only the third spacecraft to visit the planet and just the second to orbit it. It is a joint mission of the European Space Agency, or ESA, and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, or JAXA. ESA confirmed on Saturday that BepiColombo had begun its orbit. In a social media post on Sunday, ESA said the spacecraft had a successful entry into orbit, but during the maneuver, "the thruster burn was shorter than planned following a software issue."

"The spacecraft is safe and teams at ESOC (the European Space Operations Centre) are working to understand what happened," ESA said, adding that "updates will be provided on Monday." The robotic spacecraft, launched in 2018, is a composite of ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, which have different scientific objectives and are due to separate on December 9 and 10. Routine science operations are slated to commence in April. The mission will seek to answer questions about Mercury such as why it has a magnetic field, why ice exists in the polar craters of a sun-scorched planet, and what is the nature of enigmatic depressions called "hollows" on its surface. Mercury's surface looks similar to that of the moon, with numerous impact craters. There are expanses of smooth terrain as well as cliffs, some up to a mile (1.6 km) tall. Mercury is about 60 per cent closer to the sun than Earth. That means that from its surface, the sun appears more than three times as large and seven times as luminous as it does when seen from Earth. Mercury's diameter of 3,032 miles (4,880 km) is less than 40 per cent of Earth's diameter of 7,926 miles (12,753 km).

Source: Reuters

item.description: LIVERPOOL, England, Nov 22 : Mauricio Pochettino insisted Manchester United's players had shown fight and commitment despite a humiliating 4-0 defeat at Liverpool in his first game in charge, rejecting suggestions the club's dire start to the season pointed towards a relegation battle.United remain 19th in th

FAST

LIVERPOOL, England, Nov 22 : Mauricio Pochettino insisted Manchester United's players had shown fight and commitment despite a humiliating 4-0 defeat at Liverpool in his first game in charge, rejecting suggestions the club's dire start to the season pointed towards a relegation battle. United remain 19th in the Premier League table with one win from 11 games after a crushing loss at Anfield on Sunday, where Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card left the visitors facing an uphill struggle for more than 80 minutes. "We need to accept the reality and we need to be responsible, we need to be united, we need to be all together," Pochettino said, when asked what he had learned about the size of the task facing him. "What I learned from my players is that they like to fight, they commit with the team, with the club, and of course they want to win games. They want to make the effort.

"Today was a test that, for me, is very positive. After eight minutes, 10 men, red card, concede the goal in this action and then 80 minutes to play. Do you think that it's easy?" The defeat was the joint heaviest for a United manager in his first match in charge, according to Opta, equalling the 4-0 loss to Bolton Wanderers suffered by Lal Hilditch in 1926. The Argentine, who was hired after the sacking of Michael Carrick and arrived in Manchester only on Wednesday after a stint with the United States national team, said the dismissal of Yoro fundamentally altered the contest and repeatedly returned to the sending-off when assessing his side's performance. "Even the best team in the world playing like this in this situation, in our circumstance, maybe concede four goals or maybe more." Pochettino also questioned the decision itself, arguing that Liverpool striker Alexander Isak did not have the ball under control when Yoro brought him down. 'APPLAUDING RUBBISH' Former United captain Roy Keane was among those unimpressed by attempts to find positives in the defeat, questioning why the United supporters still in the stadium at the final whistle applauded the players. "Fans are applauding the players, applauding what? Applauding rubbish," Keane said. "When do the players take responsibility for some of the decision making? "Liverpool should have scored eight or nine. I feel like swearing." Pochettino, however, refused to dwell on criticism or wider questions about United's defensive record after the team conceded four goals for the third time this season across all competitions. "It's painful because it's 4-0 at the end and you lose the game. But you need to (consider) the circumstances," he said. "We are not going to lose more than one game how we lose today. We have a lot of work to do." With a Champions League trip to Portugal to face Sporting on Wednesday, Pochettino said his message in the dressing room was simple. "They are very, very, very low," he said. "But I said, 'head up, and we need to keep working, be concentrated, try to go to Portugal and try to win the game'."

Source: Reuters

item.description: Meta está “reevaluando” su objetivo de cero emisiones netas para 2030 en medio de una rápida expansión de la infraestructura destinada a respaldar la inteligencia artificial, según ha indicado la empr ...
item.dc:creator: Olivia Raimonde
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Meta está “reevaluando” su objetivo de cero emisiones netas para 2030 en medio de una rápida expansión de su infraestructura para dar soporte a la inteligencia artificial, según ha indicado la empresa en su informe anual de sostenibilidad. El gigante tecnológico informó de que sus emisiones netas de gases de efecto invernadero se dispararon un 45% el año pasado, hasta alcanzar los 11,8 millones de toneladas métricas de equivalente de carbono. El objetivo actual de la empresa de alcanzar emisiones netas cero para finales de la década se fijó en 2020, antes del rápido avance de la IA. “Cuando fijamos nuestro objetivo de emisiones netas cero, previmos un crecimiento constante, una bajada de los costes de la energía limpia y cambios en el sistema en general que permitirían avanzar al ritmo que habíamos previsto”, escribieron en el informe dos ejecutivas de Meta, Rachel Peterson y Blair Swedeen. “La realidad ha resultado ser mucho más compleja”. La demanda de centros de datos para la IA ha crecido más rápido de lo previsto y satisfacerla requiere construir a un ritmo y a una escala que el sector nunca ha intentado, escribieron. El aumento del 45% se debió principalmente a las emisiones de la cadena de suministro o de alcance 3, especialmente a los bienes y servicios adquiridos y a los bienes de capital, según indicó la empresa. Meta afirmó que ha contratado más de 30 gigavatios de energía limpia y renovable y que está invirtiendo en tecnologías bajas en carbono, como la energía nuclear avanzada y la geotérmica. Desde 2020, la empresa ha compensado todo su consumo anual de electricidad con energía limpia, principalmente a través de acuerdos de compra de energía a largo plazo y colaboraciones con empresas de suministro eléctrico. Sin embargo, su consumo de electricidad aumentó un 35% interanual a medida que se ponían en funcionamiento más centros de datos, según Meta. El gigante tecnológico ha señalado que podría recurrir al gas «behind-the-meter» para alimentar los centros de datos —lo que significa que las instalaciones no estarían conectadas directamente a la red eléctrica— si las empresas de suministro no pueden cumplir los plazos “necesarios para nuestro negocio”. Muchos promotores de centros de datos están optando por suministrar su propia energía —normalmente generada a partir de gas— para sus proyectos, ya que se enfrentan a largas esperas para las conexiones a la red eléctrica. Meta anunció en julio que está ampliando un centro de datos en la parroquia de Richland, Luisiana, hasta alcanzar los 5 gigavatios de capacidad informática, y que está financiando siete nuevas centrales eléctricas de gas natural para ello. Se prevé que al menos otros tres centros de datos estadounidenses, cuya construcción ha iniciado recientemente Meta, se alimenten, al menos en parte, de gas natural. Las grandes empresas tecnológicas han tenido dificultades para conciliar las necesidades energéticas de la IA con sus ambiciosos objetivos climáticos. Las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero de Microsoft Corp., Amazon.com Inc. y Google (de Alphabet Inc.) también se dispararon en 2025. Microsoft indicó que sus emisiones de carbono aumentaron un 25%. Las emisiones de Amazon subieron un 16%, mientras que las emisiones de Google «basadas en sus objetivos» —una definición que excluye algunas partes de su cadena de suministro— aumentaron un 18% el año pasado. En el conjunto del sector empresarial estadounidense, la inversión en iniciativas climáticas ha quedado relegada frente a otras prioridades, entre ellas la IA. Solo una cuarta parte de los responsables de sostenibilidad encuestados por el Conference Board y la empresa de análisis de datos ESGAUGE afirmaron estar seguros de que sus empresas cumplirán los objetivos medioambientales. El gigante cárnico JBS NV se retractó a principios de este año de su objetivo de cero emisiones netas para 2040, y la empresa minorista Burberry Group Plc retrasó su objetivo una década, hasta 2050. FAST

TURIN, Italy, Nov 22 : Seven-times Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz powered past world number one Alexander Zverev 6-2 7-6(7) on Sunday to win his maiden ATP Finals title. The Spaniard, who came back at the US Open after a four-month break due to a wrist injury, saved three set points in the tiebreak before completing his 14th consecutive victory and ending the year with a third straight title, having also triumphed in Vienna and Paris. The 23-year-old, who is the youngest man to have completed the career Grand Slam, secured the biggest tour title that had eluded him after finishing runner-up at the ATP Finals last year. Since losing in the quarter-finals of the US Open, he has won four titles with a 22-1 record.

"For me it's been an amazing week," Alcaraz said. "I couldn't have ended the week in a better way. I'm just really proud and really happy with everything I have done this week." "I've been through really difficult moments within myself, with my team, and we went through everything playing great tennis. This trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me." For Zverev, the defeat brought an end to his most successful season, in which he won his first two Grand Slam titles and rose to the top of the world rankings. Alcaraz initially faced little resistance from a sluggish Zverev, who had not dropped a set en route to the final. The German struggled with his usually booming serve and made 19 unforced errors in the first set. What had been billed as a blockbuster turned out to be a one-man show after Alcaraz bagged an early break to love to take control of the first set.  Zverev, a two-time ATP Finals champion, had saved all six break points he had faced during the group stage but on Sunday he was struggling to keep pace with Alcaraz from the start. The Spaniard earned five break points during the German's first two service games, converting one of them. By the end of the fifth game, Zverev had racked up 15 unforced errors. While the Spaniard buzzed around the court with his trademark intensity, chasing down every ball and nodding along to the music in the arena during the changeovers, Zverev looked sluggish and slow. He did earn one break back to cut Alcaraz's lead to 4-2 but only three points later his frustration boiled over when he argued with the umpire over a time violation warning. The second set looked to be following a similar pattern with Alcaraz keeping the level high and earning another early break. But Zverev won three games on the trot to lead 5-4 and eventually forced a tiebreak. He could not convert any of his three consecutive set points, however, before Alcaraz clinched the win.

Source: Reuters

Russia starts towing ship hit by drones in Baltic, Finland says

Finnish, Russian and Estonian vessels battle the Sparta II fire before Russia takes over the rescue as the ship heads out of Finnish waters.

Finnish Border Guard's handout photo of the Russian cargo ship Sparta II as the extinguishing of the fire continues in the Gulf of Finland November 22, 2026. Finnish Border Guard/Handout via REUTERS

FAST

HELSINKI: A Russian rescue vessel on Sunday ( Nov 22) began towing a Russian-owned cargo ship that was struck by drones in the Baltic Sea out of Finnish waters after two days of firefighting, Finland's coast guard said. The Finnish military has said the strike on the Sparta II on Saturday was likely carried out by Ukraine and that the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters. The 16 crew members were evacuated onto a nearby Russian ship. One crew member was slightly injured. "Thermal cameras show that some containers are warm, but the vessel is stable enough for towing to begin," Finland's coast guard said in a statement. It said that responsibility for the rescue will transfer to Russia once the ship leaves Finnish waters.

Pictures and video released earlier by the Finnish coast guard showed several vessels spraying the Sparta II with water cannons during the night in a bid to put out the flames and cool down containers stacked on its deck. In a rare instance of cross-border collaboration, out of the seven vessels helping to fight the fire, two were Russian, two were Estonian and the rest were Finnish. Estonia and Finland are members of NATO and steadfast supporters of Ukraine and often at odds with Moscow on other issues. Finland shut all of its land border crossings with Russia in 2023. Estonia will shut its own from December 1, for six months, on security grounds.

Related:

Russian cargo ship hit by drones in Baltic, Finland tightens security

BOUND FOR KALININGRAD The ship, bound for the Russian exclave Kaliningrad, was damaged in international waters west of Russia's Gogland island, Finland's Defence Forces have said, corroborating an account by Russian officials. "Smoke is still coming from the vessel, and there is clearly still heat on board," Jukka-Pekka Lumilahti, sea safety officer and commander of the maritime sub-centre Helsinki for the Finnish Border Guard, told a press conference earlier on Sunday. NEW DRONE ATTACKS POSSIBLE Kyiv has sent waves of military drones towards the Leningrad region on Russia's northwest coast this year, including some that strayed into the airspace of nearby Baltic countries, leading to fears that the war was spilling onto NATO territory. The risk of further attacks in the Gulf of Finland, a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea, cannot be ruled out, Estonian Navy Commander Ivo Vark told public broadcaster ERR on Sunday. Finland's military said last week it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the same area during Ukrainian drone attacks. The Sparta II is a 121-m (397-foot) Russian-flagged cargo vessel owned by Russian shipping company Oboronlogistika that left St Petersburg on Friday, according to LSEG data. Oboronlogistika provides logistics services for the Russian Defence Ministry, according to the company's website. The vessel is subject to US sanctions, according to the US Treasury Department. Lumilahti said one concern was the weather, with rain, sleet, and stronger winds expected on Sunday night and Monday.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: Una falla técnica de Delta provoca retrasos y suspensiones de vuelos en el centro de operaciones de Atlanta
item.description: Delta Air Lines Inc. suspendió temporalmente las salidas en su centro de operaciones de Atlanta el domingo después de que una falla tecnológica provocara retrasos y cancelaciones que se extendieron po ...
item.dc:creator: Sri Taylor, Jessica Nix
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Delta Air Lines Inc. suspendió temporalmente las salidas en su centro de operaciones de Atlanta el domingo después de que una falla tecnológica provocara retrasos y cancelaciones que se extendieron por toda su red; se trata del más reciente fallo de sistemas que ha complicado el tráfico aéreo en EE.UU. tras la suspensión de vuelos a nivel nacional a principios de este mes. La suspensión de salidas, que comenzó la madrugada del domingo, pasó a un programa de retrasos en tierra antes de que se levantaran ambas restricciones, según Delta. La aerolínea indicó que los empleados estaban utilizando soluciones manuales mientras los técnicos trabajaban para restablecer el sistema automatizado que se utiliza para calcular el peso y el equilibrio de las aeronaves, un paso crítico en la preparación de los vuelos para su salida. “Los equipos de Delta están utilizando soluciones manuales esta mañana para garantizar que los vuelos despeguen de manera segura mientras continúan los trabajos para restablecer el sistema automatizado”, dijo un portavoz de la empresa en un comunicado. VER MÁS: EE.UU. suspende todos los vuelos por problemas de comunicación en el control del tráfico aéreo La interrupción causó retrasos significativos durante la hora pico de la mañana en el Aeropuerto Internacional Hartsfield-Jackson de Atlanta, el centro de operaciones más grande de Delta. Solo el 50% de los vuelos de Delta programados para salir a las 7 a. m. partieron dentro de los 15 minutos siguientes a sus horarios programados, según la firma de análisis de aviación Cirium. Esa cifra cayó a alrededor del 46% para las salidas programadas a las 9 a. m., antes de recuperarse al 100% para los 65 vuelos programados para salir a las 10 a. m. Los problemas se extendieron al Aeropuerto LaGuardia de Nueva York, donde 42 vuelos de Delta con destino a ese aeropuerto fueron desviados a otros destinos el domingo por la mañana, según Cirium. Seis vuelos fueron redirigidos a Albany, Nueva York; otros seis, a Filadelfia; y cinco, a Siracusa. La aerolínea y sus filiales regionales también sufrieron una oleada de cancelaciones en LaGuardia, donde nueve de los 18 vuelos programados para salir a las 8 a. m. fueron cancelados o no operaron, junto con cinco de los 16 vuelos programados para las 9 a. m. Para los viajeros, esta interrupción significó horas de incertidumbre y cambios repetidos en los horarios de salida. Natalie Pfister, de 39 años, una agente fotográfica que viajaba a Charleston con su esposo y su hijo pequeño para pasar unas vacaciones, estaba sopesando si abandonar sus planes y volver a reservar para el lunes después de que su vuelo de Delta se retrasara cuatro horas. La aerolínea había pospuesto la hora de salida al menos tres veces, lo que dejó a la familia de Manhattan sin saber si finalmente volarían. “Cuando empiezan a retrasar y retrasar y retrasar, por lo general Delta cancela”, dijo Pfister. “Viajar por Estados Unidos es simplemente una pesadilla”. Otros pasajeros se mostraron más resignados ante la interrupción. Los jubilados Tom y Nancy Malloy, que regresaban a Florida después de un evento familiar en Nueva York, enfrentaron un retraso de dos horas y media en su vuelo a Tampa. Nancy describió los retrasos como “algo habitual al viajar hoy en día”, aunque elogió a Delta por mantener informados a los pasajeros. La pareja había atribuido inicialmente la interrupción a la niebla en el área de Nueva York y no estaban al tanto de los problemas tecnológicos en Atlanta. Esta interrupción es la más reciente de una serie de contratiempos en el transporte aéreo de EE.UU. United Airlines Holdings Inc. sufrió una falla generalizada de sus sistemas el 16 de noviembre que retrasó los vuelos de salida, apenas unos días después de que una falla de telecomunicaciones en una instalación de la Administración Federal de Aviación provocara una suspensión de vuelos a nivel nacional. La interrupción del 13 de noviembre obligó a las aerolíneas a cancelar miles de vuelos y agravó las presiones financieras sobre una industria que ya se enfrentaba a elevados costos de combustible. FAST

Nov 22 : Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara will race for Haas in the final two rounds of the Formula One season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi in a move that effectively ends his Formula Two title hopes. The 21-year-old made his F1 debut at home in Sao Paulo this month and remained in the seat for Saturday's Las Vegas Grand Prix. Camara leads Red Bull-backed Bulgarian Nikola Tsolov by seven points in the F2 standings and Ireland's Alex Dunne by 18, but will not be able to defend that advantage in the final two rounds of the support series at the Middle Eastern circuits. Brazil and Las Vegas did not feature F2 races and he cannot do both on the same weekend.

The Brazilian will start his first full F1 season with Haas next year but the opportunity to race for the US-owned team came early after they split with Esteban Ocon at the Mexico City Grand Prix, with Toyota's world endurance champion Ryo Hirakawa replacing the French driver at that race. “We’re excited to be able to finish the season with Rafa driving and build on his first two race starts with the team in Brazil and America," Haas team boss Ayao Komatsu said in a statement on Sunday. "I’m delighted that Rafa’s embraced every track session as a learning opportunity and embedded himself further within the team. We now get to finish the season together which is advantageous to us all ahead of a relatively short off-season and as our 2027 preparations get underway.” Camara finished 16th in Saturday's race after a collision with Cadillac's Sergio Perez, which brought the Mexican a five-place grid drop for Qatar.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Empresas están eliminando incentivos relacionados con el clima de la remuneración de los directivos
item.description: Verizon, Valero y Alcoa se encuentran entre las últimas empresas en prescindir de los indicadores de emisiones de carbono en sus planes de remuneración.
item.dc:creator: Ben Elgin
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Las empresas estadounidenses están eliminando cada vez más los indicadores de emisiones de carbono de los planes de remuneración de sus directivos. Solo el 17,7% de las empresas del S&P 500 vincula la remuneración de sus directivos a las emisiones de carbono, lo que supone un descenso respecto al máximo del 30% registrado en 2023, según datos facilitados a Bloomberg News por The Conference Board y la empresa de análisis ESGAUGE. Esta tendencia se ha acelerado este año, en el que 40 empresas menos del índice de referencia bursátil estadounidense han incluido dichas medidas en sus planes de remuneración. Lo mismo está ocurriendo en un sector más amplio del mundo empresarial estadounidense. Entre las empresas del índice Russell 3000, la proporción que utiliza indicadores de carbono en la remuneración de sus directivos se ha reducido casi a la mitad, pasando de un máximo del 10,3% en 2024 al 5,5% de este año. Las cifras siguen siendo superiores a las de hace cinco años, cuando muchas empresas comenzaron a incorporar dichos indicadores a sus planes de remuneración. “Las prioridades en EE.UU. han cambiado sin duda alguna”, afirma Shira Cohen, profesora asociada de contabilidad en la Universidad Estatal de San Diego, que ha estudiado los vínculos entre la remuneración de los ejecutivos y los indicadores ambientales, sociales y de gobernanza (ESG). “Las empresas parecen estar reduciendo la visibilidad y la explicitud de la remuneración vinculada al clima”. Sin embargo, según la Sra. Cohen, es demasiado pronto para saber si esto provocará un retroceso en los esfuerzos de las empresas por reducir las emisiones. “Se trata de un revés para un mecanismo de rendición de cuentas”, afirma, “pero no es necesariamente una prueba de que, en general, nuestras medidas climáticas sean más débiles”. Los datos de The Conference Board no identifican qué empresas han eliminado las medidas climáticas. No obstante, un análisis de Bloomberg News sobre la documentación presentada por las empresas reveló varios ejemplos destacados, entre ellos Verizon Communications Inc., la refinería de petróleo Valero Energy Corp. y el productor de aluminio Alcoa Corp. En Verizon, el desempeño climático había formado parte de su sistema de incentivos salariales a corto plazo durante los últimos 11 años. Verizon explicó en un documento regulatorio presentado el año pasado que la reducción de emisiones y la gestión del consumo energético podrían reducir sus costes operativos. Dicha medida ha desaparecido del informe presentado por Verizon este año. En su lugar, figura una categoría denominada “objetivos estratégicos y culturales”, que evalúa a los ejecutivos en función de objetivos tales como ganarse la confianza de los clientes, empoderar a los empleados e impulsar la productividad. Valero introdujo un cambio similar. Durante varios años, la refinería utilizó un “modificador de transición energética” que podía aumentar o reducir parte de la remuneración incentivada de los ejecutivos hasta en un 25%, en función de los avances en la reducción de emisiones y la producción de combustibles con menor contenido de carbono. Valero afirmó este año que dicha medida había contribuido a impulsar inversiones en negocios como el combustible sostenible para la aviación. Sin embargo, eliminó el modificador, alegando, en parte, las “condiciones adversas” a las que se enfrentan las inversiones en negocios con bajas emisiones de carbono. Verizon se negó a hacer comentarios, y Valero no respondió a los mensajes. Alcoa, que también eliminó un indicador de intensidad de carbono de su plan de remuneración de ejecutivos, se negó a hacer comentarios. Este reciente retroceso se produce tras años de ataques por parte de los republicanos contra la inversión ESG y las iniciativas climáticas corporativas. Desde que el presidente Donald Trump regresó a la Casa Blanca, su administración ha promovido los combustibles fósiles y ha revocado numerosas normas y políticas relacionadas con el clima. Los fiscales generales estatales republicanos también han puesto en el punto de mira o amenazado a empresas de contabilidad, empresas tecnológicas y grupos de defensa por diversas actividades relacionadas con el clima durante los últimos dos años. Al mismo tiempo, muchas de las principales gestoras de activos, como BlackRock Inc., se han mostrado más discretas respecto a la necesidad de que las empresas reduzcan sus emisiones. “Los consejos de administración y la dirección se han enfrentado, sin duda, a menos presión para demostrar sus compromisos climáticos”, afirma Andrew Jones, director del Centro de Gobernanza y Sostenibilidad de The Conference Board. A principios de este año ya se vislumbraban indicios de este retroceso. Apple Inc., por ejemplo, eliminó discretamente una cláusula ESG que permitía a su consejo de administración ajustar las bonificaciones anuales de los altos ejecutivos hasta en un 10% en función de los resultados de la empresa en indicadores como la reducción de gases de efecto invernadero, según informó Bloomberg News. Dicha cláusula, vigente desde 2021, tuvo consecuencias reales para los bolsillos de los ejecutivos: aumentó la remuneración del entonces director ejecutivo, Tim Cook, en casi 750.000 dólares en 2023. Apple ha afirmado que mantiene su compromiso con sus objetivos medioambientales. “Se puede considerar que los indicadores de remuneración reflejan la forma en que una empresa prioriza lo que realmente importa”, afirma Jannice Koors, directora general sénior de Pearl Meyer, una consultora especializada en remuneración de ejecutivos. “Lo que se mide, se hace”. Sin embargo, no toda la desaparición de un indicador climático supone necesariamente una declaración política. Koors señaló que las empresas también han descubierto que vincular los planes de incentivos a un problema que se prolonga durante décadas puede resultar complicado. Una empresa puede comprometerse a alcanzar un objetivo de emisiones en 2030 o 2035 —años después de que algunos de los ejecutivos a los que se recompensa hoy en día hayan dejado sus puestos. Por lo tanto, es posible que algunas empresas estén reajustando sus estrategias tras descubrir lo difícil que resulta diseñar incentivos climáticos que realmente funcionen. “Creo que, cuanto más se adentraban las empresas en este tipo de indicadores, más defectos descubrían”, afirma Koors. “Estas medidas pueden resultar realmente difíciles de aplicar correctamente”. No obstante, el retroceso en los incentivos climáticos sigue siendo modesto, en comparación con el colapso de las medidas de diversidad corporativa. En 2023, el 58,1% de las empresas del S&P 500 vinculaban parte de la remuneración de sus ejecutivos a la diversidad y la inclusión. Este año, solo lo hace el 10,4%. Esos incentivos han sido objeto de un intenso escrutinio, ya que la Administración Trump ha investigado prácticas de diversidad más amplias en empresas como Nike Inc. y Lockheed Martin Corp., alegando que algunas de ellas dieron lugar a una discriminación ilegal. International Business Machines Corp. acordó en abril pagar 17 millones de dólares para resolver dichas acusaciones del Departamento de Justicia de EE.UU., aunque negó haber cometido ninguna irregularidad. “En el espacio de unos pocos años, la DEI en los planes de remuneración de los ejecutivos simplemente ha desaparecido”, afirma Jones, de The Conference Board. “Existe la percepción de que estas métricas entrañan un riesgo jurídico real”. LIVERPOOL, England, Nov 22 : The scale of Mauricio Pochettino's rebuilding job was laid bare on Sunday as Manchester United crashed to a 4-0 Premier League defeat at Liverpool, their first match under the Argentine unravelling within minutes. Reduced to 10 men after eight minutes, United fell two goals behind within 13 and never recovered as Liverpool cruised to victory through goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, teenager Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz. United's nightmare start to the Pochettino era could hardly have been worse as Leny Yoro was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak, and the visitors paid the price moments later when Szoboszlai curled home the resulting free kick. Liverpool doubled their lead three minutes later when Ngumoha beat Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz, who finished with an acrobatic volley, swivelling and firing home while turning his back to goal.

The goal had Liverpool fans chanting "Sacked in the morning!" at United's new 54-year-old manager, who had arrived in England only four days earlier following his spell with the United States national team. The Reds attacked in waves after the break and the 18-year-old Ngumoha added a third in the 66th minute, sweeping home a cross from Bradley Barcola to become the youngest player to score in a Premier League match between Liverpool and United. Substitute Munoz added to United's misery when he fired home a ball from Wirtz, sending United fans streaming towards the exits. The few who were left by the final whistle serenaded the United players with Bob Marley’s “Three Little Birds” and its hopeful refrain: “Every little thing is gonna be all right.” "So, so painful. So disappointed," Pochettino said. "It's not in your head to start here in the Premier League in this situation. The only problem was that the game changed completely after (eight) minutes and now we can talk and explain everything, but the damage is done. "The players are feeling the pain of this type of situation. I told them they need to be calm and it was a completely unfair situation that happened." Liverpool climbed to fourth on 21 points, seven behind leaders Arsenal, while beleaguered United are 19th with just eight points and one victory to show from 11 games. RECORD-EQUALLING DEFEAT Pochettino is only the second of the Red Devils' last 10 managers, including caretakers, to lose his first league game in charge after Erik ten Hag. It was the joint heaviest defeat for a United manager in his first match in charge, according to Opta, equalling the 4-0 loss to Bolton Wanderers suffered by Lal Hilditch in 1926. United's winless league run is their worst since they went 11 games without a win between November 1989 and February 1990. Liverpool, meanwhile, ran roughshod over United all afternoon, recording 27 shots - including a remarkable 12 on target - to their visitors' 11, and had 15 corners to United's five. "It was definitely important today, also the table situation," said Wirtz. "A lot of teams at the top didn't win this weekend so it's good we can use the chance. "The red card influenced the game of course, but we take that. We earned that because of the run of Alex (Isak), so it's very good." Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola had kind words for Wirtz, who created 10 chances. "He's in a lovely moment and we want to keep him there as much as we can," Iraola said. "He's in a situation against 10 players where you need players like him to control the situation and see the passes in behind. "He's also arriving more and not just scoring but being a threat. He's becoming another option and I'm happy with him."

Source: Reuters

item.title: AI Rout Turns Gold Into Source Of Cash: What Comes Next?
item.description: Gold fell to a 14-month low on Friday as a rout in technology shares prompted investors to sell bullion to cover losses elsewhere. The metal slid alongside falling Treasury yields and the US ...
item.content:encoded:
News / Benzinga / AI Rout Turns Gold Into Source Of Cash: What Comes Next?

AI Rout Turns Gold Into Source Of Cash: What Comes Next? 2 min read

QQQ NEM B AEM Gold fell to a 14-month low on Friday as a rout in technology shares prompted investors to sell bullion to cover losses elsewhere. The metal slid alongside falling Treasury yields and the US dollar. Spot gold fell to $3,502 an ounce- the lowest level since September 2025. In total, bullion lost 8.9% for the week, while the Invesco QQQ ETF QQQ sank 9.31% and State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF (NYSE:SPY) fell by 7.98%, entering correction territory Rate Hike Bets Set the Stage Minutes from the Federal Reserve’s October meeting showed that nearly all policymakers anticipated further rate increases . According to the CME FedWatch , traders currently price in an 88.6% chance of a quarter-point increase in December. “The ongoing AI-related equity selloff is prompting some forced liquidations of gold positions to cover losses,” David Meger , director of metals trading at High Ridge Futures, told Reuters. Ole Hansen , head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank, wrote that bullion “has become a source of cash for investors facing mounting losses elsewhere,” Mining.com reported. In a market commentary, former Bridgewater economist Bob Elliott said pro-growth pricing “remains quite elevated” and warned the selloff could become “more self-reinforcing to the downside.” Once downturns start, he wrote, they typically require “both much cheaper pricing and some sort of policy support to get to the bottom, neither of which we are at yet.” Interestingly, there was little sign of a broad exit from gold funds. Holdings in gold ETFs tracked by Bloomberg were little changed over the preceding month despite a roughly 10% drop in bullion, Hansen said. Mining shares were less resilient, since their leverage to gold price works both ways. The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (NYSE:GDX) closed the week 14.80% below the previous Friday’s close. The largest names in the sector, Newmont NEM , Barrick Mining B and Agnico Eagle Mines AEM lost 15.03%, 15.19% and 13.64%, respectively. Technical Outlook Gold’s daily chart shows the magnitude of the post-summer carnage. After peaking in August and briefly moving above the 200-day moving average, bullion reversed course and fell by over 25%.

Gold, daily chart, Source: TradingView Zooming out, the next key support area is the Q2-Q3 2025 price range. For much of that time, price remained in a tight accumulation between $3,200 and $3,450. Thus, price could easily fall further, test that range, and wait for the next catalyst to move it either way.

FAST

WASHINGTON, Nov 22 : Americans should expect more technology outages and disruptions as companies and government agencies replace aging systems, the top US intelligence official said on Sunday. "And as part of that ongoing upgrade, we are going to have glitches, gaps, interruptions in service," Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNN's "State of the Union" program. "That is going to happen." Clayton was interviewed on Sunday morning news programs days after President Donald Trump attributed a recent spate of technology failures to upgrades of companies' technology systems. Clayton said the upgrades were necessary to improve performance and cybersecurity as technological advances strain older systems. A string of technology failures this month disrupted critical US systems, including a nationwide halt to air travel, a Microsoft outage that hit email services, a technical glitch that affected several major banks and a temporary disruption to the National Security Agency's network.

Clayton declined to discuss specifics of separate reports of cyberattacks on the FBI and Department of Agriculture, saying he expects investigators to provide answers "in due course."

Nov 22 (Reuters) – Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on Sunday they had carried out an operation targeting Saudi Arabia’s Rabigh oil refinery on the kingdom’s western Red Sea coast, as they continued to claim attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure.

The Houthis said they had achieved a direct hit but there was no indication of what damage had been inflicted and the Saudi authorities did not immediately comment.

Rabigh is home to Petro Rabigh, a major integrated oil refining and petrochemical complex developed by Saudi Aramco and Japan’s Sumitomo Chemical. It is located about 165 km north of Jeddah on the Red Sea coast and has access to deep-water export facilities.

Show Full Article

The Houthis have repeatedly claimed attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure in recent months, including the East-West oil pipeline and refineries in Jazan in the south and Ras Tanura in Eastern Province. Saudi authorities have not confirmed any attacks on refineries.

The renewed fighting, which began in July amid the wider US-Israeli war with Iran, has seen the Houthis seize territory from Yemen’s internationally recognised government and step up missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports and energy infrastructure.

Saudi Arabia has also intensified airstrikes against Houthi positions in support of its Yemeni allies.

(Reporting by Hatem Maher and Ahmed Tolba; Editing by Susan Fenton and David Holmes)

By Katharine Jackson WASHINGTON, Nov 22 (Reuters) – The US is seeking answers from Nvidia on its chip sales to China and will find out who was in charge of compliance at the company formerly led by Jensen Huang, who resigned following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday.

“We’ve been in touch with the temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do need answers. … It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was,” Bessent told the CBS program “Face the Nation.”

Reports about Huang’s relationship with a woman whom US intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy and his extramarital affair with a company executive led to his resignation and investigations by US regulators and the FBI, congressional action, an internal review and a proposed investor class-action lawsuit.

Show Full Article

Days after Huang’s resignation, President Donald Trump’s administration issued a rule to further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips from companies like Nvidia, tightening controls ahead of Trump’s trip to China last week for talks with President Xi Jinping.

Bessent said the chipmaker’s board of directors is working to determine what had happened, and he expressed confidence that it would “come up with some very fulsome and robust answers.”

“We do need to see who was in charge of compliance there,” Bessent said. “We will see which level of the business knew about this. Was it at the lower levels? Was it at the middle level? Did it go all the way to the top?”

Trump said on Friday that he would like to see Huang apologize and return to Nvidia. Asked whether he agreed with Trump, Bessent said more information is needed.

“I think we have to see where the buck stops,” Bessent said.

Nvidia board Chairman Harvey Jones has said the board will not rehire Huang.

(Reporting by Katharine Jackson; Editing by Sergio Non, Will Dunham and Bill Berkrot)

item.title: Trabajadores con visado H-1B están hartos y abandonan los puestos de trabajo en el sector tecnológico estadounidense
item.description: Las nuevas tasas y los retrasos exasperantes están empujando a los profesionales cualificados a abandonar el país ...
item.dc:creator: Francesca Maglione, Alicia A. Caldwell
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Yash Sharma decidió el mes pasado que ya había tenido suficiente de Estados Unidos. Este ingeniero de software de Google, de 36 años y originario de la India, afirma que, a mitad del segundo mandato de Donald Trump, los constantes cambios normativos en materia de visados para inmigrantes altamente cualificados, la incertidumbre que generan y las escasas posibilidades que tiene de obtener la ciudadanía se han convertido en una carga insoportable. Sharma, que lleva seis años con un visado H-1B, afirma que le resulta difícil concentrarse en el trabajo. Y aunque le encanta su vida en San Francisco y trabajar en el epicentro de la tecnología y la inteligencia artificial, siente que se ha quedado sin opciones para obtener la residencia permanente y labrarse una vida aquí. Estados Unidos le parece una “prisión dorada”, afirmó Sharma. Tiene previsto trasladarse al Reino Unido el próximo mes, aunque allí no tenga trabajo, porque le han ofrecido un visado que le abre un camino claro para permanecer en el país a largo plazo. Las elecciones de mitad de legislatura de este mes supusieron un revés para la política de mano dura de Trump en materia de inmigración, lo que ayudó a los demócratas a hacerse con el control del Congreso y llevó al presidente a reconocer que su administración podría haber sido “demasiado dura” a la hora de deportar a personas que tenían empleo. Sin embargo, se ha prestado menos atención a la reforma de las normas sobre visados llevada a cabo por la Administración, normas que durante años han facilitado la incorporación de titulados universitarios y trabajadores altamente cualificados al mercado laboral. A la oposición, recién fortalecida, no le resultará fácil revertir los cambios normativos de Trump, que han desmantelado de hecho un sistema de inmigración que contribuyó a convertir a Estados Unidos en un destino para los mejores ingenieros e investigadores del mundo. Precisamente esta semana, el Departamento de Trabajo ha propuesto normas más estrictas para las empresas que deseen patrocinar a trabajadores extranjeros para la residencia permanente. Algunas de las mayores empresas estadounidenses están renunciando a la idea de que algo vaya a cambiar pronto. International Business Machines Corp. va a poner fin al patrocinio de visados estadounidenses para la mayoría de los puestos de trabajo de su división más grande, lo que obliga a los empleados afectados a trasladarse fuera de EE.UU. o a plantearse abandonar la empresa antes de que termine el año. La empresa de pagos Flywire Corp. está sopesando la posibilidad de trasladar más actividades de contratación y desarrollo al extranjero, mientras que a Microsoft Corp., Adobe Inc. y a un puñado de empresas de externalización de IT se les ha prohibido participar en un programa clave de patrocinio de tarjetas de residencia, mientras las autoridades federales investigan sus prácticas. La Administración Trump afirma que los trabajadores y los empleadores han abusado del sistema de inmigración durante años, alejándolo de sus orígenes —como vía para atraer al país, de forma temporal, a talento altamente especializado— y convirtiéndolo en un coloso desmesurado que ha dado lugar a salarios más bajos para los estadounidenses. Las investigaciones sobre cómo afectan los inmigrantes a los salarios han arrojado resultados dispares. Sin embargo, un estudio publicado recientemente por un economista de la Universidad de Harvard que formó parte del Consejo de Asesores Económicos de Trump reveló que la inmigración cualificada conduce a una reducción de los salarios de los trabajadores estadounidenses con estudios universitarios, especialmente en los ámbitos científicos. El nombramiento este mes por parte de Trump de Stephen Miller como jefe de gabinete otorga mayor autoridad a este defensor de larga data de la reducción de todas las formas de inmigración, mientras que las investigaciones sobre los patrocinios de tarjetas de residencia por parte de los empleadores, anunciadas el mes pasado por el vicepresidente JD Vance, han aumentado la presión. “Se trata de un desmantelamiento silencioso de la inmigración basada en el empleo”, afirmó Angelo Paparelli, abogado especializado en inmigración y socio de Vialto Law. Existe una sensación cada vez mayor de que la fricción y la imprevisibilidad son la nueva normalidad para el sistema de inmigración de EE.UU. Esto está modificando las previsiones sobre el futuro de la economía estadounidense y obligando a las empresas a planificar para un mundo en el que quizá no puedan traer a los mejores talentos para que trabajen en sus sedes centrales de EE.UU. “Las economías de escala son un tema delicado. Es un poco como la reputación: puede llevar años construirla y un instante destruirla por completo”, afirmó Scott Corley, director ejecutivo de Compete America, una coalición de las principales empresas estadounidenses del sector tecnológico y de profesionales altamente cualificados. Sharma afirma que se ha sentido desanimado ante las posibilidades de poder convertir algún día su visado temporal en residencia permanente, dada la enorme acumulación de solicitudes pendientes para los ciudadanos indios. No ha salido del país en un año y medio, por temor a no poder volver a entrar. Esto le ha supuesto perderse visitas familiares, conferencias de trabajo y viajes con amigos. Buscó otra vía para obtener la residencia permanente y una mayor estabilidad solicitando un visado por “capacidad extraordinaria”, concedido a personas con un talento destacado en su campo, pero su solicitud fue denegada tras meses de espera. La incertidumbre llevó a Sharma a plantearse una vida fuera de EE.UU. Solicitó un visado de «Talento Global» del Reino Unido y se le concedió, lo que le permitió trasladarse al Reino Unido sin tener un empleo y empezar a buscar trabajo. Afirma que los resultados de las elecciones estadounidenses no le han disuadido de su plan. “He visto varias administraciones y, para mí, está claro que no habrá ningún cambio real en la ley”, afirmó. E incluso si las cosas volvieran a ser como antes, la dificultad para obtener la residencia permanente seguiría pesándole. “Esa normalidad sigue siendo un fastidio”, afirmó. La amplia campaña de Trump contra la inmigración comenzó casi inmediatamente después de que asumiera el cargo. Tras hacer campaña con la promesa de acabar con la inmigración ilegal, la red de control se amplió para restringir las vías de inmigración legal, añadiendo nuevas regulaciones y tasas elevadas. En septiembre del año pasado, el popular programa de visados H-1B para trabajadores extranjeros altamente cualificados pasó a ser el centro de atención, primero con un decreto presidencial que exigía un pago de 100.000 dólares a determinados candidatos a un puesto de trabajo que se encontraran fuera de EE.UU. En agosto, a pesar de una orden judicial que bloqueaba ese pago original, el Gobierno decidió imponer una tasa independiente de 103.000 dólares para las nuevas solicitudes de visado H-1B. Muchos de los cambios políticos de Trump se enfrentan a impugnaciones legales, pero el caos y la confusión resultan difíciles de gestionar tanto para las empresas como para los trabajadores. Swapnil Deshpande, que trabaja como analista de datos sénior en una importante empresa tecnológica estadounidense, afirmó que los constantes cambios en la política de inmigración han hecho difícil imaginar un futuro estable en EE.UU. Este ciudadano indio llegó en 2018 para cursar un máster en la Northeastern University y lleva casi seis años trabajando en Nueva York. Cada día se despierta con la sensación de que podría ser su último día en EE.UU. Según cuenta, hace dos años tenía una idea más o menos clara de cómo serían sus próximos cinco años. Quizá formaría una familia, compraría una vivienda y se establecería aquí. Pero en los últimos dos años, ese plan se ha vuelto difuso. “Tanto mi esposa como yo queríamos comprar una casa y comenzar una nueva etapa, pero ahora la pregunta que nos hacemos es: “¿Qué va a pasar el mes que viene o mañana? ¿Dónde acabaremos? ¿Qué nos depara realmente el futuro?”, afirmó. “¿Merecen realmente la pena la incertidumbre, el estrés y la imprevisibilidad?“. Las empresas también se están replanteando cómo contratan a algunos de los trabajadores extranjeros más solicitados. IBM comunicó este mes a sus empleados que dejaría de patrocinar a trabajadores extranjeros para la mayoría de los puestos de su división de consultoría, según un documento compartido con los directivos y al que ha tenido acceso Bloomberg News. Para Flywire, con sede en Boston, unas normas de inmigración más estrictas podrían dificultar la contratación de los ingenieros que desarrollan sus sistemas de tecnología de pagos. La empresa, que gestiona miles de millones de dólares en pagos al mes para universidades y otros clientes, afirmó en un informe trimestral presentado este mes que está considerando “reubicar las actividades de contratación y desarrollo en jurisdicciones de menor coste en las que ya operamos” para compensar el aumento de los costes de los visados H-1B. Advirtió de que las dificultades para contratar y retener a especialistas podrían ralentizar el desarrollo de sus propios productos, mientras que un menor número de estudiantes extranjeros que elijan universidades estadounidenses supondría una reducción de los ingresos por matrículas que pasan por su red. Los datos comienzan a reflejar el impacto de las restricciones impuestas por Trump. Durante el ejercicio presupuestario de 2025, que incluyó los tres últimos meses completos de la administración Biden, Estados Unidos expidió unas 260.000 visados temporales de no inmigrante menos que el año anterior, según los datos federales sobre visados analizados por el Instituto de Política Migratoria. La matriculación internacional en las universidades estadounidenses ha disminuido, con una caída estimada del 15% en el número de nuevos estudiantes extranjeros este otoño, según el Instituto de Educación Internacional. La participación en el Programa de Formación Práctica Opcional (OPT), que otorga a los estudiantes internacionales un permiso de trabajo temporal, se redujo un 6% al inicio del curso académico 2026-27, lo que supone el primer descenso en cinco años. Chris Thomas, abogado especializado en inmigración y socio del bufete Holland & Hart en Denver, afirmó que sus clientes empresariales le preguntan por los riesgos a los que se enfrentan si deciden contratar a extranjeros. Para muchos de ellos, la idea es: “Sabemos que estamos llevando a cabo los controles adecuadamente, sabemos que cumplimos con la ley, pero la preocupación es que nos puedan acusar de todos modos”, señaló. Añadió que muchos clientes temen que cualquier error percibido pueda llevar al Gobierno a excluirlos de los programas de visados de trabajo o a iniciar investigaciones penales. Y, a largo plazo, señaló, algunos de sus clientes empresariales se preguntan si merece la pena lidiar con las complicaciones que supone intentar desenvolverse en un panorama migratorio basado en el empleo cada vez más complejo. “Algunos afirman que es demasiado, que es hora de empezar a deslocalizar”, señaló Thomas. Aunque los recursos judiciales podrían limitar el alcance de las restricciones de Trump, Thomas y otros señalaron que ya se ha extendido la percepción de que la Administración está haciendo que Estados Unidos sea un país menos acogedor. “Esto genera una profunda inestabilidad en todo el ecosistema de la inmigración”, afirmó Kate Angustia, asesora supervisora de políticas y prácticas de la Asociación Americana de Abogados de Inmigración. “Estamos provocando una fuga de cerebros”. --Con la colaboración de Brody Ford, Emily Flitter y Carolyn Silverman. FAST

HULL, England, Nov 22 : Hull City manager Sergej Jakirovic hailed his side's collective effort after they earned their first Premier League victory since August with a 2-0 win over Brighton & Hove Albion on Sunday, thanks to an injury-time double from Oli McBurnie. The result ended promoted Hull's eight-match winless run and lifted them further clear of the relegation zone with 14 points from 11 games, while preventing Brighton from cutting the gap to leaders Arsenal. "We played against an excellent team today, very high intensity," Jakirovic told Sky Sports. "We won 2-0 and I'm extremely happy because we wait almost three months (for another win) which is unbelievable, but I have never been in the Premier League before."

GOALKEEPING MASTERCLASS KEEPS BRIGHTON AT BAY Hull were forced to withstand sustained pressure early on, with goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis producing a string of superb saves to preserve parity. The Greek stopper made five saves in the first half, including a brilliant one-handed stop from Diego Gomez's effort in the 15th minute, helping Hull survive before they grew into the contest after the break. "In the first half we survived and Konstantinos Tzolakis saved us four or five times. We had more stability in the second half," Jakirovic said. Brighton's task became harder when Joao Costinha was sent off late on after collecting a second yellow card, and McBurnie made the extra man count, striking twice in stoppage time to seal a smash-and-grab victory. "I never had doubt in Oli McBurnie because I know what he means to the team," Jakirovic added. "We have to create chances for McBurnie and he will score. No matter if we win or lose, it is always a good atmosphere in the dressing room." BRIGHTON RUE WASTED OPPORTUNITIES Brighton manager Fabian Huerzeler lamented his side's wastefulness after they failed to convert their chances despite controlling large spells of the game. "That's football. The Premier League is ruthless. Hull scored with a lucky punch, we have to accept it and be better next time," Huerzeler told Sky Sports, adding that his side lost intensity after the 65th minute. "We rushed things, we lost a bit of intensity, we tried to force things because we weren't patient enough," he said. "You can easily get frustrated if you miss so many chances." Brighton host Newcastle United next Sunday, when Hull visit Crystal Palace.

Source: Reuters

US intelligence chief says Putin is ‘not America’s friend in Ukraine’

By John Kruzel WASHINGTON, Nov 22 (Reuters) – Russian President Vladimir Putin is not a friend when it comes to Ukraine, US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on Sunday, days after President Donald Trump spoke warmly of Russia’s leader.

“He is not America’s friend in Ukraine,” Clayton told ABC News’ “This Week” program. “Not at all.”

Asked about Trump’s recent description of Putin as a friend, Clayton also said the term was “entirely appropriate” in the context of discussions among leaders of the world’s three leading nuclear powers — the United States, Russia and China — during last week’s high-profile summit in China.

Show Full Article

Trump defended calling Putin a friend on Thursday, saying that “it’s nice to have people that have 4,000 nuclear weapons as a friend as opposed to an enemy.” But when asked about the subject again on Friday, Trump declined to say whether Putin is a friend to the United States as a whole: “I can’t speak to America.”

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and controls about a fifth of the country’s territory. Putin has shown no sign of dropping his demand that Ukraine surrender all of its eastern Donbas region in exchange for peace.

Trump’s description of Putin as a friend drew criticism from European allies of Ukraine. “Mr Putin is not our friend and will never be,” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said.

Asked on Thursday about Trump’s remarks, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy shrugged and walked away.

(Reporting by John Kruzel; Editing by Sergio Non and Bill Berkrot)

FAST

Nov 22 : Augsburg forward Michael Gregoritsch scored twice as his side beat Mainz 05 3-1 at home in Germany's Bundesliga on Sunday, overcoming the sending-off of their coach Manuel Baum to record their third win of the season.  Gregoritsch gave his side the lead in the 19th minute and Juma Bah added a second before Baum was red-carded for holding onto the ball to prevent Mainz midfielder Nadiem Amiri from taking a quick throw-in two minutes before the break.  Undeterred, Gregoritsch scored again three minutes into the second half, and though substitute Ransford Konigsdorffer pulled a goal back for Mainz shortly afterwards, that was as close as they came as Augsburg held on for a much-needed win.  The victory lifted Augsburg past Mainz and up to 10th place in the standings on 12 points after 10 games, with their visitors slipping to 13th on 10 points. In Sunday's late kick-off, Justin Njinmah grabbed a quick-fire double in the middle of the second half as Werder Bremen secured a 4-0 home win over Hamburg that leaves them sixth in the table on 18 points, six ahead of Hamburg, who are 12th.

Source: Reuters

Most business continuity plans are inward-looking, focused on internal networks and data centres rather than third-party failures, according to industry experts.

FAST

Nov 22 : If Marc Marquez's 2025 MotoGP title ended a painful six-year wait, his record-equalling eighth premier-class crown a year later provided an even more compelling demonstration of his refusal to surrender. Marquez overturned a 102-point deficit, the largest in MotoGP history, and recovered from injuries and two operations to climb from eighth in the standings and wrap up the championship in Portugal with a round to spare. The title drew him level with Giacomo Agostini on eight premier-class championships and took him clear of Valentino Rossi, whose bitter rivalry with the Spaniard became one of the sport's most polarising storylines. "Incredible! I need to smile. It was a season where I adapted to different circumstances. I understood in the first part of the season that the instinct was not working anymore," Marquez said.

"At one point even I felt that it was over, but the people around me - the team, my brother, girlfriend, family and Ducati - always believed in me. "They said, 'Please finish races and your moment will arrive'. And that's what I did." REBUILDING AN INJURY-HIT CAMPAIGN Marquez had already proved that he could win titles with his sheer speed and racecraft. This season required something different: the resilience to rebuild his campaign, recover from major setbacks and outthink an entire grid. There were legitimate concerns about whether the 33-year-old could return to his best, let alone challenge for another world title after undergoing two operations, on his shoulder and on a fractured foot. He rebuilt his campaign methodically, however, rediscovering the rhythm, confidence and attacking edge needed to unlock the Ducati's full potential. Seven rounds into the 2026 season, Marquez was without a single race win as the reigning champion looked out of sorts against a resurgent Aprilia's two-pronged attack of Jorge Martin and Marco Bezzecchi. Aprilia clearly had the faster bike at several circuits, but having two title contenders can be a mixed blessing. Ducati, by contrast, could focus support on Marquez as team mate Francesco Bagnaia struggled. Aprilia held the upper hand after Marquez crashed in the French Grand Prix sprint in May, an accident that led to the double surgery and forced the Spaniard to miss his home Catalan Grand Prix. "If I come back with the mentality that I can win this championship, I will be injured again," Marquez had said ahead of his return at the Italian Grand Prix in May. MARQUEZ SURGES UP THE STANDINGS After testing his physical limits in Italy, however, Marquez revived his challenge by winning six of the next nine rounds to surge up the standings. After Bezzecchi's own injury problems cost him the championship lead, Aprilia threw their weight behind Martin as the 2024 champion sought to leave the team on a high before his switch to Yamaha next season. By the time the paddock left Australia last month, however, Marquez had moved clear of Martin, who then missed the Malaysian Grand Prix with a fractured wrist to hand his compatriot a further advantage. "I tried to control my instincts. That was the biggest problem of my career," Marquez added. "And it's true that my instinct also gave me the chance to fight for a unique championship." Martin has won only one race in an injury-disrupted season, while Bezzecchi, who dropped to third in the standings, suffered costly setbacks at crucial moments. "Aprilia lost the championship because they fought against Marc. If not, it's impossible," Marquez's brother and Gresini Racing rider Alex said. Aprilia's internal rivalry handed Marquez an opening and he exploited it expertly, piling pressure on his rivals with his performances on the track and psychological manoeuvring in the paddock. When Martin suggested earlier this month that Marquez was the only one who could win or lose the championship, the Ducati rider confidently retorted with a smile: "They're the only ones who can lose it." And so, against two Aprilia challengers who had threatened to run away with the championship on a superior bike, Marquez used all his experience and guile to complete his coronation in Portugal, bringing his career full circle in the country where he took his first steps in motorcycle racing 18 years ago. With the shadow of a goat following him on the giant screen behind him, Marquez climbed a staircase in a theatrical nod to his "Greatest of All Time" credentials before Agostini presented him with a golden helmet, a fitting image of two riders at the summit of motorcycle racing.

Source: Reuters

FAST

BARCELONA, Nov 22 : Barcelona shook off a sloppy first half to beat Villarreal 3-2 in LaLiga on Sunday, coming back from two goals down against their opponents, who were reduced to 10 men. After a nightmarish start for Hansi Flick's side, a fading Villarreal could not cope with a persistent and fiery Barcelona in the second period. Barcelona remain top of the standings on 36 points, three ahead of Real Madrid after Jose Mourinho's side beat Celta Vigo on Saturday. Villarreal remain ninth on 15 points. Tajon Buchanan took just two touches to convert Fermin Lopez's lax giveaway into the opening goal for Villarreal after five minutes.

Alberto Moleiro released Tani Oluwaseyi into space on the left flank and the Canadian international added Villarreal's second with a powerful finish two minutes later. Even as Barcelona began to create chances, their game was plagued by errors, characterised by Lamine Yamal winning a penalty and then dragging it onto the post in the 23rd minute. Barcelona's comeback was finally ignited by Gerard Martin, who headed in a quickly taken short corner in the 57th minute. Pedri provided the cross for Martin's goal and was picked out for special praise by Flick after a dominant performance. "(His) game today was one of the best," Flick told a press conference. "How he controlled the midfield, how managed our game, increased the tempo, it was amazing." Fermin Lopez finished a brilliant move to level the score in the 61st minute. Centre-forward Raphinha had sprinted to the right-back spot to thwart a counter-attack and was involved again in a sequence that finished with Lamine Yamal finding Fermin on the left side of Villarreal's box. With Barcelona hungry for a third, what seemed like a mountainous task was completed in a matter of 10 minutes. Lamine Yamal's cross from the right was turned across the line by Villarreal defender Pau Navarro inside his own six-yard box. "When we're playing like this, the opponent gets tired," Flick said. "The second half was unbelievable how we played football, this hunger to come back and to score the goals, it was fantastic." Navarro was sent off in stoppage time for a second yellow as Barcelona saw out the victory.

Source: Reuters

LAS VEGAS, Nov 22 : Formula One stewards handed Mexican Sergio Perez a five-place grid penalty for next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix after ruling the Cadillac driver caused a collision with Haas' Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara in Las Vegas on Saturday. • Perez would have collected a 10 second penalty but because he had retired from the race it was changed to a grid drop for his next race instead • The stewards said Perez had not earned the right to the corner and was wholly to blame for the lap 18 collision on approaching turn 14 • "I was alongside him and expected him to leave me enough room to make the corner," said Perez. World

Climate deal collapses in chaotic end to COP31

COP31 talks in Antalya break down after nearly 200 nations fail to bridge splits over fossil fuels, leaving no cover decision and no US$120 billion climate goal.

COP31 President Murat Kurum speaks during the plenary session at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye on Nov 22, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Murad Sezer)

22 Nov 2026 10:38PM (Updated: 23 Nov 2026 05:05AM)
